ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, P is a point outside the circle $\odot O$. The tangents PA and PB are drawn from P to $\odot O$. If $\angle APB=50^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\overset{\frown}{AB}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since PA and PB are tangents to the circle O,\\
it follows that $\angle PAO=\angle PBO=90^\circ$,\\
and since $\angle APB=50^\circ$,\\
then $\angle AOB=360^\circ-\angle APB-\angle PAO-\angle PBO=130^\circ$,\\
thus, the degree measure of $\overset{\frown}{AB}$ is $\boxed{130^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with center O on the right. Point P is outside the circle on the left. Two segments from P touch the circle at A and B, forming tangents PA and PB. The radii OA and OB are drawn, so the quadrilateral P-A-O-B is visible in the diagram. Reasoning: Since PA and PB are tangents to the circle, the radius to each point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent. Therefore ∠PAO = 90° and ∠PBO = 90°. The given angle is ∠APB = 50°. In quadrilateral P-A-O-B, the angles sum to 360°, so ∠AOB = 360° - 90° - 90° - 50° = 130°. The measure of minor arc AB equals the measure of its central angle ∠AOB, so arc AB measures 130°.
